articles.title: Which issues matter most to American voters in the midterm elections?
articles.summary: The BBC spoke to voters across the US about their biggest electoral priorities when casting their ballots.
articles.body:
What issue matters most to US voters in this year's midterm elections?

The BBC spoke to voters from California, Texas, Michigan, Illinois, Arizona, Missouri, Oklahoma, Colorado, Alabama, Nebraska, Florida, Tennessee, Wisconsin, Virginia, Maryland, New Jersey and New York about their top issue.

Voters cited concerns over the economy, the immigration crackdown, fears of the country becoming either fascist or communist, among other issues.

Interviews gathered and filmed by Meiying Wu, Angélica Casas, Blanca Estrada, Sheila Flynn, Katy Bailes, Pratiksha Ghildial and Andrew Sarge Herbert

Has Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil to evade justice?

The BBC's Ione Wells looks at whether the defeated right-wing presidential candidate travelled to the US to avoid an ongoing criminal investigation.

What we know as Flávio Bolsonaro lands in US after Brazil election loss

The BBC's Ione Wells unpacks Bolsonaro's journey to Miami after losing Brazil's presidential election and facing a passport surrender order.

'I earned the respect': First woman football captain at University of Manitoba

Maya Turner was recently named one of the University of Manitoba's seven captains, becoming the first woman to hold the position in the school's history.

Watch: 'It's part of the culture' - New York bans horse-drawn carriages after more than 160 years

The BBC's Madeline Halpert spoke to city tourists, residents and horse carriage workers about the industry and their opinion on the ban.

Damaging hail pelts Phoenix in rare storm

Videos from the Arizona capital show people sheltering inside a car as hail smashes the windscreen, while intense downpours covered neighbourhoods in ice.

Watch: How Trump's mass deportation drive is playing out in Ohio

The BBC's Tom Bateman traveled to Springfield to see how President Donald Trump's immigration policies are affecting the community.

'Let's move on': Albertans react to separatist movement setback

Preliminary referendum results show that more than two-thirds of Alberta voters support remaining part of Canada, easing concerns over national unity.

The father and son on opposite sides of Alberta’s separation vote

Albertans are voting on whether to stay in Canada or pursue independence via a referendum, splitting even some close-knit families.

Every scrap of paper checked: Police hunting for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail

BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as America battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

Community 'heartbroken and horrified' after Oregon school shooting

A 16-year-old killed three children and a teacher at a primary school in Oregon before he was killed by a bystander, police say.

How did Katie Zacharia do at her first - very brief - White House briefing?

The BBC's Sarah Smith was in the room and describes Zacharia's performance and the moment she broke news about Kimberly Guilfoyle being asked to resign.

Watch: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released

A series of calls, obtained by the Associated Press, reveal emergency services were delayed in reaching Pike.

Watch: US man eyes pumpkin world record after fifth contest win

Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California where he won the annual event.

BBC on the scene as agents search Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home

The BBC's Ione Wells reports from outside the Minnesota representative's home as several immigration agents were seen carrying boxes from the house to a van.

Storm Rachel batters Southern California, brings flooding to Las Vegas

Large waves from the post-tropical cyclone battered homes in Long Beach, and brought flooding to parts of Las Vegas near the famed Strip.

Could Alberta's vote on independence be Canada's Brexit moment?

WATCH: The BBC's Nadine Yousif meets the separatists who want to quit the country - and the Canadians calling for unity in the face of threats from US President Trump.

BBC breaks down video of the aftermath of New York City ICE shooting

The BBC's Nada Tawfik goes through new dramatic body cam footage that shows the tense moments when police arrive on scene.

Watch: 'I am Jane Doe' protests across US call for end to sexual violence

Protests against sexual violence took place across more than 40 US states on 8 October.

Hurricane Isaias strengthens as it heads towards land

Isaias will bring damaging winds, torrential rain and a storm surge with landfall expected late Friday.

What Americans think about the death penalty

The BBC spoke to Americans and international tourists in Washington DC about their views on the death penalty following the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.

articles.title: POST SCRIPT | Rotinomics: The Tyranny of the Phulka
articles.summary: The defining sound of the North Indian dinner is not conversation.
articles.body: The defining sound of the North Indian dinner is not conversation. It is the soft slap of dough passed from palm to palm, then the hiss of a phulka ballooning over an open flame, then, a few seconds later, a voice from the kitchen asking whether anyone would like one more. Everyone would like one more, which is rather the point of a phulka, since it must be eaten within a minute or so of its birth before it collapses into something limp and apologetic. Somebody therefore has to stand at the tawa while everybody else sits, and in a great many homes between Amritsar and Ahmedabad, that somebody has her dupatta tucked into her waist and has not yet had her dinner.Rice does not work like this. Rice is cooked once, carried to the table in a single vessel and left there, steaming and indifferent, for everyone to help themselves, the cook included. Rice does not need a woman hovering over it. Rice, you might say, is the more democratic grain.I offer this as a theory, by which I mean a dinner-table provocation that has since done some reading. The reading turns out to be more supportive than I expected, and also, as reading tends to be, more inconvenient.A line no cartographer would drawTake a map of India and a ruler, and draw a straight line from Gangtok to Goa. No cartographer would draw such a line, which is precisely why a columnist should. North and west of it lie Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and the Himalayan states; south and east of it lie Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, the two Telugu states, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and the whole of the North-east. Chhattisgarh, with an indecision I find touching, sits more or less on the line itself, while Bihar is sliced diagonally, with Patna on one side and Purnia on the other, which will surprise nobody who has eaten in both.The line is crude, but it is not arbitrary, because it follows with embarrassing fidelity the oldest culinary border in the country. In 11 states, according to the 2022-23 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey, wheat makes up more than half of all the cereal people eat, and the heaviest wheat-eaters per head are Rajasthan, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Punjab. Punjab does grow rice, mountains of it, but it grows rice the way Switzerland makes watches, largely for other people: economists at Punjab Agricultural University have noted that roughly three-quarters of the state's rice has gone into the central pool for decades. North of the line, rice is something you ship. South of it, rice is something you eat, twice a day, from a pot that sits in the middle of the table and waits for nobody.The case for the prosecutionNow look at what happens to girls on either side of the line. The cleanest measure available is the child sex ratio from the 2011 Census, the last one completed, which counts girls per thousand boys under the age of seven, and, on a map of India, it does not so much suggest a pattern as draw one.Haryana, at 834, brings up the rear, followed by Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir and Delhi, and the shading lightens almost obediently as one travels south and east. Among the large states, the separation is total: the best performer on the roti side is Bihar, at 935, a state that eats as much rice as wheat, while the worst on the rice side, the undivided Andhra Pradesh of 2011, still manages 939. One small north-eastern state, Manipur, spoils the perfection at 930, as small states will, but social science so rarely hands you a line this clean that the proper response is suspicion, to which I shall come.Women's work, at least where the prosecution has chosen to look, tells a similar story. In 2022-23, according to Periodic Labour Force Survey figures tabled in the Lok Sabha, Delhi had the lowest female labour force participation of any state or union territory, at 14.8 per cent, with Haryana at 20.7 and Punjab at 27.6, while Chhattisgarh, on the line, reached 59.8 and Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Odisha all cleared 44. Punjab and Haryana being among the richer states in the country, it is not poverty that keeps their women at home. Something else does.That something is visible at dinner. When the World Food Programme studied poor households in Fatehpur and Lucknow in 2019, it found the order of service long settled: husbands, children and the elderly first, the women last, after everyone else had eaten their fill, a rule that applied equally to pregnant and breastfeeding women. Neither the men nor the women regarded this as discrimination; the women defended it on the grounds that the men went out to work. The phulka, in other words, is not the cause of anything. It is merely the clock by which the waiting is measured.The economists got there firstI would like to claim this theory as my own, but scholars have been circling the line for half a century, usually from the field rather than the kitchen. In 1970, the Danish economist Ester Boserup argued that the plough, involving heavy work that favoured male strength, pushed women out of farming and into the home, and four decades later, Alberto Alesina, Paola Giuliano and Nathan Nunn found that the descendants of plough-using societies still take a narrower view of a woman's place. In 1974, Pranab Bardhan, writing in the Economic and Political Weekly, observed that girls fared better in India's rice regions, where transplanting paddy has always needed women's hands, than in its wheat regions, where it has not. Barbara Miller's The Endangered Sex and a celebrated 1983 paper by Tim Dyson and Mick Moore drew the same map from another direction: the north marries its daughters into distant villages and cuts them off from their own people, while the south keeps them nearer their kin and, the authors argued, gives them more say.The newer work is sharper and, if anything, bleaker. Eliana Carranza of the World Bank showed in 2014 that districts with loamy soils, which permit deep ploughing and so need fewer women in the fields, have fewer girls than districts of heavy clay, where women's labour is still wanted; a daughter, in the arithmetic of the agrarian household, is worth roughly what her labour is worth. Gautam Hazarika, writing in the Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization in 2024, calls rice the odd plough crop out, so hungry for labour that it has always needed women, and finds that the habit has outlived the paddy: urban women are more likely to work in districts better suited to rice than to wheat, an effect that shows up only among women native to the district, while urban housewives in wheat country are more likely to say they are required to stay at home. The field, it seems, follows a woman into the city long after she has stopped transplanting anything.Even China has been called as a witness. Thomas Talhelm's 2014 study in Science found rice-growing southern China more interdependent in its thinking than the wheat-growing north, which turned out to be more individualistic. That last finding would puzzle anyone raised in a north Indian joint family, where individualism has traditionally been a privilege reserved for the eldest man at the table, who is, naturally, the one being served first. The economists, in short, blame the plough. My modest contribution is to move the crime scene from the field to the kitchen and to name the tawa as an accessory.The case for the defenceThe trouble with a theory this pleasing is that it is pleasing, and the defence has a strong case, which it may as well open with my own people. In the 2023-24 National Family Health Survey, released this year, the large state with the highest share of young women married before 18 is West Bengal, at 36.4 per cent, followed by Bihar at 34.6, Assam at 25.3 and Andhra Pradesh at 25.1, while Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh come in at 10.2, 11.9 and 13.7. On child marriage, the roti side wins, and wins handsomely; Kerala, at 2.9 per cent, remains the rice side's best alibi. Nor is the Bengali dinner the democratic affair my theory requires, since it arrives in courses, shukto and dal and bhaja and macher jhol and chutney in strict liturgical order, and somebody has to stand and serve every one of them. Rice may be democratic. The fish head is a hereditary monarchy, and it passes down the male line.The prosecution's labour figures, it must be admitted, were chosen by a columnist. The same 2022-23 survey puts Rajasthan at 47.9 per cent and Gujarat at 42.3, well ahead of West Bengal at 33.8 and Assam at 20.3, and the highest female participation of any state belongs to Himachal Pradesh, at 71.4; across the large states, the median on either side of the line sits at about 40 per cent, which is to say that on this measure the line all but vanishes. I was briefly cheered to learn from the National Sample Survey that Himachal eats more rice than wheat, until I noticed how quickly a spoiler had become evidence, which is the precise moment at which a theory should be taken outside and questioned, and until I noticed that Jammu and Kashmir, which eats more than twice as much rice as wheat, has the third-worst child sex ratio on my own map. Rajasthan's women, meanwhile, are a reminder that working in the fields is not the same thing as being excused from the tawa; a great many women do both, in that order, every day.The sex ratio, my star exhibit, is less obliging than it looks. The 2011 Census is now fifteen years old, and the civil registration figures for 2023 put Jharkhand (899 girls per 1,000 boys at birth) and Telangana (906), both on the rice side, alongside Bihar (900) at the bottom of the table, with Haryana, at 911, merely joint sixth from the bottom, though registration in several of these states is still patchy. The historians are unkind too. James Fenske, Bishnupriya Gupta and Cora Neumann, rebuilding sex ratios from the colonial censuses of 1881 to 1931, confirm that the north skewed male long before anyone owned an ultrasound machine, but find its link with wheat and rice weaker than the literature has claimed, and Lupin Rahman and Vijayendra Rao concluded in 2004 that economics, the state and restrictions on women's movement explain the north-south gap better than kinship does. Lines on maps, it turns out, are drawn in pencil.The casserole solutionNone of this proves that a flatbread oppresses anybody. Bread has no opinions, and the phulka, for all its theatrical puffing, has never once asked who is holding the tongs. What the line suggests, rather, is that a household arranges its food around whoever it has already decided can wait, and the phulka merely makes the arrangement easier to see, because the person doing the waiting is standing up.The remedy is not to abolish the phulka, which would be a crime against civilisation, nor to convert the north to rice, which Punjab is in any case too busy growing for the rest of us. North India already owns the technology of its own liberation: the insulated casserole, that pastel hot-case on every middle-class dining table from Ludhiana to Lucknow, which allows the rotis to be made in one batch and carried to the table the way rice is, so that the cook can sit down with everyone else. The roti will be a degree or two less heroic. The dinner will be considerably more just.Alternatively, and I say this as a man who has eaten more than his share of first phulkas, the person who wants one more could get up and make it.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Flight canceled? Experts share 7 tips for getting rebooked and avoiding extra costs.
articles.summary: Travel experts explain what to do when your flight is canceled, from understanding your rights to securing a seat on a new flight while minimizing expenses.
articles.body:
There's a very specific, sinking feeling travelers know all too well: It sets in when you find out your flight was canceled .

As frustrating as this can be, you have more control than you might think over how things play out. The steps you take immediately afterward can determine how quickly you resume your journey and how much the disruption may ultimately cost you. That's especially true during the busy holiday season, when flights are in high demand and seats are limited.

But it's not just about reacting quickly — strategy is equally important. We spoke with travel experts about what to do when a flight cancellation throws a wrench in your plans, from understanding your rights to securing a seat on a new flight while minimizing unexpected expenses.

Here are seven steps to get your travels back on track.

First things first: You might be able to get ahead of a cancellation before it's officially announced — if you know what to look for. Matt van Arnhem, airline pilot and founder of the AI-powered flight-delay prediction service DelayGuard , tells Yahoo Travel that "creeping delays" (repeated postponements) are the top warning sign.

If the underlying cause is a maintenance issue with the plane, van Arnhem says engineers might be hopeful they can fix it, only to find it's more complicated than expected. Or the crew could be waiting on a delayed aircraft, but then run out of legally permitted working hours, with no standby crew available to take over.

Van Arnhem advises using your airline's app or a flight-tracking service to watch your incoming plane. If your departure is scheduled within the next hour but your aircraft hasn't even left its previous airport, it could point to the possibility of a cancellation or, at the very least, significant delays.

If it seems a cancellation is increasingly likely, proactively search for alternative flights and check your airline's travel alerts for waivers. You may be able to switch to an earlier flight and dodge the disruption before it even happens. Just make sure you don't forfeit your existing seat until you've confirmed your replacement itinerary.

Experts say the first thing you should do after receiving a cancellation notification is to check the airline's app. Whether you know it or not, your airline may have rebooked you automatically, and the app is typically the fastest way to find out if this happened.

Even if the airline hasn't rebooked you yet, you can often look for alternative flights and change the itinerary yourself without having to wait for an agent to help you in person or on the phone.

Marshall Jones, an expert at the online travel agency and flight concierge service Catchaflight , advises taking a screenshot of the cancellation notice in case you need that documentation for a travel insurance claim or reimbursement later on.

Jones also recommends simultaneously calling customer service or getting in line at the customer service desk while you're using the app to research alternative flights.

"Have two workable flight numbers ready so you can ask for something specific," he adds. "Once one channel confirms your new ticket, stop the others from making competing changes."

3. Don't automatically accept (or reject) a new flight

Sure, an automatic rebooking may be the simplest solution. But before you move forward, it's worth comparing all the details, including the arrival time, destination airport, connections and seating arrangements.

"I'd ask, 'Am I confirmed and ticketed, or only on standby?' Then check whether bags, paid seats, assistance requests and onward or return flights are covered," advises Jones.

If the new flight doesn't work for you, make sure to ask about alternate options before you give up your seat, says van Arnhem, because declining a replacement flight is a gamble. You could find a more favorable itinerary, but you could just as easily end up with a less convenient option.

Just make sure to check if your airline set a deadline to accept or decline the new flight.

If your airline's next available flight won't get you to your destination in time, consider expanding your search to alternative airlines, connecting flights or nearby departure and arrival airports.

Just don't forget to factor in any necessary ground transportation: A flight that lands earlier can still cost you hours if it leaves you a long drive away from where you're staying, says Jones.

According to Aman Thakran, founder of the U.K.-based travel agency BharatFare , airlines can sometimes handle the rebooking for flights operated by partner carriers. So, if you find an available seat on a different airline, he recommends sharing the flight number with an agent and asking whether they can book it for you before you buy a replacement ticket yourself.

It doesn't matter whether the flight was canceled due to weather, a plane malfunction or something within the airline's control. If you choose not to take the alternative offered to you, you're generally entitled to a refund under U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) rules if your flight was to, from or within the U.S.

And as tempting as it may be in a panic, don't automatically accept a travel voucher, says Anton Radchenko, CEO of the flight claims management company AirAdvisor : DOT rules dictate that you're entitled to a refund to your original payment method. However, if you can't delay your travel plans, Jones cautions against rushing to request a refund.

"A refund returns the unused ticket's value, which might be far less than a last-minute fare," he explains.

If you do opt for a refund, the airline must issue it automatically within seven business days of the refund becoming due if you paid by credit card, or within 20 calendar days if you used another payment method.

Many airlines in the U.S. have committed to providing meal vouchers, complimentary overnight hotel stays and ground transportation to or from the hotel when a flight cancellation happens due to situations within their control, like crew shortages, certain technical problems, cabin cleaning or refueling issues.

These commitments often don't apply, though, when a cancellation is due to events like extreme weather or airport closures.

If you end up stranded overnight because of a canceled flight, Jones advises asking for assistance before booking a hotel yourself, and clarifying what will happen to checked baggage.

Be sure to keep itemized receipts for any meals, lodging, transportation or other purchases you make as a result of your canceled flight. You may be able to get reimbursed by the airline, your travel insurance or a credit card for those out-of-pocket expenses. And you generally need some form of documentation to support your claim.

7. Review your travel insurance and credit card benefits

If you have a travel insurance policy — or paid for your flight with a credit card that offers travel protection — check whether those benefits might reimburse certain expenses, like lodging or meals, says Arhan Chhabra, president of the travel rewards platform Rove .

Whether you're eligible for reimbursement usually depends on the reason for the disruption, coverage limits and how long you're delayed. Keep in mind that you may need written confirmation of the cancellation and its cause from the airline in order to file a claim.

articles.title: PS Câmara de Portel: 27 vagas com salários de até R$ 4,7 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Edital prevê 27 vagas imediatas e cadastro de reserva para cargos de níveis fundamental, médio, técnico e superior. Inscrições começam nesta quinta-feira, 29.
articles.summary: O concurso Câmara de Portel oferece 27 vagas imediatas para diversos níveis de escolaridade, com inscrições abertas de 29 de outubro a 15 de novembro de 2026.
articles.body:
A Câmara Municipal de Portel , no arquipélago do Marajó, abriu Processo Seletivo com 27 vagas imediatas e formação de cadastro de reserva para cargos de diferentes níveis de escolaridade. Os salários básicos variam de R$ 1.621 a R$ 4.723,31.

O PS é organizado pelo Instituto Vicente Nelson. A jornada de trabalho prevista é de 30 horas semanais para todos os cargos.

As oportunidades são para funções administrativas, operacionais e especializadas do Legislativo municipal. Há vagas para candidatos com ensino fundamental completo, ensino médio ou técnico e ensino superior.

Para candidatos com ensino fundamental completo, há vagas para:

Quem tem ensino médio ou formação técnica pode concorrer aos cargos de assistente administrativo, assistente de plenário, auxiliar técnico de áudio, vídeo e sistemas, condutor marítimo, guarda legislativo, intérprete de Libras, motorista, ouvidor, técnico de informática e técnico legislativo.

Nesse grupo, são três vagas para assistente administrativo, três para técnico legislativo e duas para guarda legislativo. Os demais cargos têm uma vaga cada.

Para quem possui ensino superior, o edital prevê uma vaga para cada uma das seguintes funções:

Além das vagas imediatas, haverá cadastro de reserva para os cargos previstos no edital. Os candidatos classificados poderão ser convocados durante o prazo de validade do concurso, conforme a necessidade da Câmara e as regras da seleção.

Os maiores salários básicos, de R$ 4.723,31, são destinados aos cargos de advogado legislativo e assistente social. Para controlador interno, a remuneração prevista é de R$ 3 mil.

Já para os cargos de níveis fundamental, médio e técnico, o vencimento básico informado no edital é de R$ 1.621.

Os candidatos devem consultar o edital para conferir os requisitos e as atribuições específicas de cada função.

As inscrições serão feitas exclusivamente pela internet, no site do Instituto Vicente Nelson, até 15 de novembro de 2026.

As taxas de inscrição variam conforme o nível de escolaridade exigido para o cargo:

Candidatos inscritos no Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais do Governo Federal (CadÚnico) e integrantes de famílias de baixa renda poderão solicitar a isenção da taxa entre 29 de outubro e 3 de novembro, desde que atendam aos critérios previstos no edital.

A seleção terá prova objetiva de múltipla escolha, de caráter eliminatório e classificatório, prevista para 29 de novembro de 2026, no município de Portel.

Os candidatos aos cargos de nível superior também passarão por avaliação de títulos, de caráter classificatório.

Após a homologação do resultado final, os aprovados deverão comprovar que atendem aos requisitos exigidos para o cargo e realizar exames médicos.

O concurso terá validade de dois anos a partir da homologação do resultado final, com possibilidade de prorrogação por mais dois anos, uma única vez.

articles.title: Alerta amarelo prevê tempestade para Mato Grosso do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Aviso do Inmet vale até o fim desta quinta-feira (29) e prevê chuva intensa, ventos de até 60 km/h e risco de alagamentos, quedas de galhos e descargas elétricas em todo o estado.
articles.summary: Aviso do Inmet vale até o fim desta quinta-feira (29) e prevê chuva intensa, ventos de até 60 km/h e risco de alagamentos, quedas de galhos e descargas elétricas em todo o estado.
articles.body:
Todos os 79 municípios de Mato Grosso do Sul estão sob alerta amarelo de chuvas intensas nesta quinta-feira (29). O aviso foi emitido pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ) e segue válido das 9h até as 23h59. A previsão indica chuva entre 20 e 30 milímetros por hora, podendo chegar a 50 milímetros ao longo do dia, além de ventos entre 40 km/h e 60 km/h.

Segundo o Inmet, há baixo risco de corte de energia elétrica, queda de galhos de árvores, alagamentos e descargas elétricas. O alerta é classificado como de perigo potencial.

De acordo com a Climatempo, a combinação de calor, umidade e a atuação de uma instabilidade atmosférica favorece a formação de áreas de chuva em diversas regiões do estado. As precipitações podem ganhar força ao longo do dia, com possibilidade de temporais isolados.

Nas áreas em alerta, as rajadas de vento durante as tempestades podem atingir até 70 km/h. Além disso, raios, chuva intensa e ventania podem reduzir a visibilidade nas estradas, dificultar o trânsito e provocar alagamentos pontuais.

Na sexta-feira (30), a instabilidade continua sobre Mato Grosso do Sul. As pancadas de chuva devem ocorrer de forma mais irregular, com maior possibilidade de intensificação nas regiões norte e centro-leste.

As temperaturas máximas previstas para sexta-feira (30) são:

Já no sábado (31), o calor e a umidade seguem favorecendo a formação de nuvens carregadas. A chuva deve começar pela manhã nas regiões norte e leste, podendo ocorrer com intensidade moderada a forte e acompanhada de temporais isolados. No sul e sudoeste do estado, o tempo tende a ficar mais estável, embora não estejam descartadas pancadas localizadas.

O Inmet recomenda alguns cuidados durante as rajadas de vento:

Não se abrigar sob árvores, devido ao risco de queda e descargas elétricas;

Não estacionar veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda;

Evitar o uso de aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada;

Em caso de emergência, acionar a Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo telefone 193.

articles.title: PixMEI de R$ 5 mil será via app e sem devolução, diz ministro | G1
articles.standfirst: Dinheiro será concedido a fundo perdido, ou seja, sem necessidade de devolução e sem cobrança de juros. Recurso deverá ser usado na compra de máquinas, equipamentos e ferramentas profissionais, além de melhorias na estrutura do negócio.
articles.summary: Com foco em 1,5 milhão de empreendedores, o PixMEI de R$ 5 mil será liberado via app para compra de equipamentos sem juros ou necessidade de devolver o recurso.
articles.body:
O ministro do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte (MEMP), Paulo Pereira, informou nesta quinta-feira (29) que o chamado "PIXMei" de até R$ 5 mil, anunciado durante a campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva à reeleição , deverá ser implementado por meio de aplicativo para que o acesso seja facilitado.

O dinheiro será concedido a fundo perdido, ou seja, sem necessidade de devolução e sem cobrança de juros.

O recurso deverá ser usado na compra de máquinas, equipamentos e ferramentas profissionais, além de melhorias na estrutura do negócio, segundo a regras do programa.

Em entrevista ao programa "Bom dia, ministro", da EBC, Paulo Pereira lembrou que, como o valor de até R$ 5 mil será disponibilizado para os microempreendedores individuais realizarem investimentos para aumentar sua capacidade produtiva, ou seja, para melhorar seus negócios, será necessário apresentar a nota fiscal da compra realizada posteriormente.

"São investimentos de até R$ 5 mil, não precisam ser de R$ 5 mil, que possam aumentar capacidade produtiva. É a primeira vez que a gente faz na história do Brasil. Brasil faz subvenção ao agro, indústria, mas ninguém tinha feito ao empreendedor. A gente está preparando em um valor específico, de 1 a 1,5 milhão de MEIs,. Se der certo, a gente pode fazer isso de maneira permanente'", afirmou o ministro do Empreendedorismo.

Paulo Pereira avaliou, na entrevista, que "nem todos os MEIs vão pedir o dinheiro", pois "nem todos vão ter projetos de investimentos".

"Vamos testando, vamos ter uma linha específica para empreendedoras, para os MEIs que faturam menos, os 'nanoMEIS'. Vão ter critérios para ir construindo as políticas públicas", acrescentou o ministro.

Ele lembrou que o PIXMei não está disponível neste ano, que ele será ofertado somente a partir de 2027, e observou que já há fraudes na internet pedindo cadastramento de microempreendedores para o acesso ao benefício.

O ministro pediu que os MEIs tenham atenção para não cair em golpes, pois as regras do programa ainda não saíram e ainda não há cadastramento ativo iniciado.

articles.title: Aulas são suspensas em Itapeva após identificação de parasita na água  | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão abrande as redes municipal e estadual e foi informada pelas redes sociais da prefeita Adriana Duch Machado (MDB), na noite desta quarta-feira (28). Análise do Adolfo Lutz apontou organismos que aparecem na água com coliformes fecais contaminados.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Itapeva cancelou as aulas da rede municipal e estadual, nesta quinta-feira (29), após a identificação de um parasita na água.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Itapeva (SP) cancelou as aulas da rede municipal e estadual de ensino, nesta quinta-feira (29), após uma análise feita pelo Instituto Adolfo Lutz apontar um parasita na água que estava abastecendo a população. A cidade chegou a registrar 2,6 mil casos de gastroenterite em apenas 20 dias.

A decisão do cancelamento das aulas foi informada através das redes sociais da prefeita Adriana Duch Machado ( MDB ), na noite desta quarta-feira (28). De acordo com o comunicado, a medida busca preservar a saúde dos estudantes, professores e servidores.

O resultado das análises foi divulgado pelo instituto da capital paulista por meio de nota encaminhada à TV TEM nesta quarta-feira (28). O documento aponta que foi encontrado na água o protozoário Cryptosporidium spp .

Prefeitura de Itapeva cancela aulas municipais e estaduais nesta quinta-feira (29) — Foto: Redes sociais/Reprodução

Através do comunicado, a prefeitura também orientou os moradores a preferirem água envasada ou fervê-la por cinco minutos, manter a higiene dos alimentos e das mãos, e também acompanharem os canais oficiais do município.

Caso os moradores apresentem sintomas, a orientação da Prefeitura de Itapeva é que procurem uma Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) para receber o tratamento médico adequado.

As aulas foram canceladas após a identificação de um parasita na água em Itapeva — Foto: Redes sociais/Reprodução

Na análise clínica feita nos pacientes, além do protozoário Cryptosporidium spp ., foi encontrada a bactéria Escherichia coli enteroagregativa , transmitidos na água contaminada com coliformes fecais.

🔎 O protozoário Cryptosporidium spp. afeta as células do intestino delgado e pode ser transmitido pela ingestão de água ou alimentos contaminados com fezes de humanos ou animais infectados. Ele causa diarreia intensa, cólicas, náuseas, vômitos e febre.

🔎 Já a Escherichia coli enteroagregativa adere às células da mucosa intestinal e secreta toxinas que danificam o intestino. A transmissão ocorre da mesma forma e causa diarreias líquidas, mal-estar e febre baixa, que podem durar mais de duas semanas e causar danos na absorção de nutrientes.

Devido às anomalias, a Secretaria Estadual de Saúde de São Paulo (SES-SP) fez uma reunião com a Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (Sabesp), com o intuito de adotar as medidas necessárias para a normalização da água fornecida na cidade.

Em nota, a Sabesp informou que acesso, nesta quarta-feira, aos resultados divulgados pela Secretaria Estadual da Saúde sobre a identificação de microrganismos em duas amostras de água coletadas em 19 de outubro em uma praça pública de Itapeva.

A companhia afirma que análises de 227 amostras de água coletadas pela companhia no município entre 1º e 27 de outubro indicaram conformidade com os padrões de potabilidade estabelecidos pela legislação vigente.

Como medida, a companhia disse que fará análises de amostras adicionais e a renovação da água por meio de descargas de rede para reforçar a segurança e a qualidade da água e dar tranquilidade à população.

A TV TEM entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Itapeva para solicitar esclarecimentos, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

A Secretaria Estadual de Saúde de São Paulo (SES-SP) enviou 40 mil frascos de hipoclorito de sódio à população, após outras análises apontarem alterações na qualidade da água encanada da cidade.

Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

🔎 O hipoclorito de sódio é um desinfetante químico, amplamente utilizado para desinfecção e saneamento. Ele elimina bactérias, vírus e parasitas, tornando a água segura para beber.

O município registrou, em cerca de 20 dias, 2,6 mil casos de virose na saúde pública . Os resultados apontaram alterações de cloração, cor e turbidez entre 22 de setembro e 7 de outubro, período em que os atendimentos médicos foram registrados.

Como orientação da Secretaria, a população deve consumir alimentos bem cozidos, higienizar corretamente as mãos antes de preparar alimentos e usar hipoclorito de sódio a 2,5% para desinfecção da água.

Apesar das alterações, a Sabesp afirmou, também via nota, que não identificou anomalias na água encanada em Itapeva.

A apuração da administração municipal começou após 700 pessoas apresentarem sintomas semelhantes em apenas quatro dias. Entre os principais relatos estão vômito e diarreia.

O aumento da procura também foi percebido em uma farmácia da cidade, que precisou reforçar o estoque de medicamentos usados no tratamento desses sintomas.

A Câmara Municipal de Itapeva abriu, na segunda-feira (26), uma Comissão Especial de Inquérito (CEI) para investigar a qualidade da água distribuída pela Sabesp.

O grupo que forma a comissão terá 90 dias para investigar a companhia pela qualidade da água oferecida à população. O requerimento de abertura da CEI foi assinado por 11 parlamentares, com cinco compondo a mesa. Veja os integrantes abaixo :

A investigação começará no dia 4 de novembro, com previsão de término entre o fim de fevereiro e o início de março de 2027, devido ao recesso legislativo em janeiro.

Câmara Municipal de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo a Câmara, a CEI servirá para entender se houve falha no tratamento e no abastecimento de água, além de entender como isso está relacionado ao surto de gastroenterite.

Saiba quais são os sintomas de gastroenterite — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A gastroenterite é uma inflamação do estômago e do intestino e pode provocar sintomas como diarreia, vômito, náuseas, dores abdominais e febre.

Conforme a Secretaria de Saúde de Itapeva, na maioria dos casos, a recuperação pode ocorrer em casa, com alguns cuidados. A principal recomendação é manter a hidratação, consumindo água, soro de reidratação e outros líquidos ao longo do dia para repor a quantidade perdida pelo organismo.

A alimentação também deve ser mantida, dando preferência a alimentos leves e de fácil digestão, como sopas, frutas e torradas. O repouso é indicado enquanto persistirem os sintomas.

Outro cuidado importante é a higiene das mãos, principalmente após ir ao banheiro e antes de preparar ou consumir alimentos. A medida ajuda a reduzir o risco de transmissão da doença para outras pessoas da casa.

A Secretaria de Saúde também orienta que medicamentos sejam utilizados somente com indicação médica.

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3077: aposta de Sergipe acerta a quina e outras 34 ganham a quadra; veja cidades | G1

articles.summary: Uma aposta simples de Rondonópolis, em Mato Grosso, levou a faixa principal.
articles.body:
Uma aposta feita em Aracaju acertou cinco números do concurso 3.077 da Mega-Sena , realizado na noite de quarta-feira (28), e faturou R$ 32.185,33. O prêmio principal para quem acertasse as seis dezenas era de R$ 324,8 milhões e saiu para uma aposta simples de Rondonópolis (MT).

Em Sergipe, além da quina, 34 apostas acertaram quatro números. Os valores recebidos variam de R$ 701,94 a R$ 4.211,76, de acordo com a quantidade de números jogados e o formato do jogo (individual ou bolão).

Veja os números sorteados: 02 - 14 - 18 - 31 - 35 - 40.

Confira a quantidade de apostas premiadas na quadra por município:

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

Volantes da Mega-Sena — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer / Agência Brasil

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online . Para concorrer, é necessário ter mais que 18 anos de idade.

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Rússia testa míssil nuclear intercontinental disparado por submarino | G1
articles.standfirst: Míssil balístico Bulava, de alcance superior a 8 mil km, atravessou todo o território russo e caiu em uma área de testes no estado de Arkhangelsk. Teste ocorre em meio a tensões com a Europa e temores de uma nova escalada da guerra no Irã.
articles.summary: Míssil balístico Bulava, de alcance superior a 8 mil km, atravessou todo o território russo e caiu em uma área de testes no estado de Arkhangelsk. Teste ocorre em meio a tensões com a Europa e temores de uma nova escalada da guerra no Irã.
articles.body:
A Rússia testou nesta semana um míssil balístico intercontinental nuclear em meio a uma escalada de tensões com a Europa e temores de uma nova escalada da guerra no Irã.

O Ministério da Defesa russo informou na quarta-feira (28) que disparou um míssil RSM-56 Bulava a partir de um submarino nuclear Generalissimo Suvorov que estava localizado no mar de Okhotsk, no extremo leste.

O projétil viajou uma distância de cerca de 8,3 mil km, atravessando quase todo o território da Rússia , e caiu em uma área de testes no estado de Arkhangelsk, no noroeste do país.

"O submarino nuclear estratégico de mísseis balísticos Generalíssimo Suvorov lançou um míssil balístico intercontinental Bulava, conforme o plano de treinamento, e confirma prontidão para combate", afirmo a pasta em comunicado.

O órgão russo não afirmou se o míssil estava carregado com uma ogiva nuclear, porém isso seria incomum em testes como esse, que costumam utilizar apenas uma ogiva comum.

O míssil RSM-56 Bulava tem um alcance de 8,3 km e capacidade para carregar uma ogiva nuclear de focos múltiplos e com capacidade de gerar explosão 10 vezes mais poderosa que a Little Boy, usada pelos EUA em Hiroshima. Um submarino russo da classe Borei, como o Generalissimo Suvorov, é capaz de carregar até 16 projéteis do tipo Bulava.

Lançamento deste do míssil balístico nuclear intercontinental Bulava a partir de um submarino nuclear submerso. Foto de arquivo. — Foto: Ministério da Defesa da Rússia via CSIS

O lançamento do míssil Bulava, que já foi testado em outras ocasiões nos últimos anos, ocorre em um momento de tensões entre a Rússia e a Europa, por conta da guerra da Ucrânia e de incidentes híbridos em território europeu, como o drone de ataque no aeroporto de Leipzig, na Alemanha. A Otan vem se rearmando ultimamente diante do que chama de ameaça russa.

Além disso, atualmente há temores de uma nova escalada da guerra no Irã, com a mídia dos EUA reportando que o governo Trump estaria planejando a retomada de amplos ataques contra o país do Oriente Médio, o que poderia desencadear uma expansão sem precedentes do conflito e arrastar outros países.

No início do mês, a França testou um míssil balístico nuclear do tipo M51.3 no Mar do Norte, no que o presidente Emmanuel Macron chamou de "mensagem em alto e bom som".

Na semana passada, a Dinamarca comprou seus primeiros mísseis de precisão de longo alcance para, segundo Copenhague, "reforçar suas defesas e aumentando o poder de combate em uma situação de segurança grave e em deterioração".

Rússia testa míssil balístico nuclear intercontinental Bulava a partir do submarino nuclear Generalissimus Suvorov no mar de Okhotsk em 28 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Ministério da Defesa da Rússia

articles.title: Paraná volta a entrar em alerta de tempestades com chuvas e ventos fortes; veja onde temporais devem ser mais intensos | G1
articles.standfirst: Inmet emitiu avisos de chuvas intensas nesta quinta (29) e sexta-feira (30). Veja também como fica o fim de semana.
articles.summary: Inmet emitiu avisos de chuvas intensas nesta quinta (29) e sexta-feira (30). Veja também como fica o fim de semana.
articles.body:
O Paraná voltou a entrar em alerta de tempestades com chuvas e ventos fortes nesta quinta (29) e sexta-feira (30). O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu avisos sobre o perigo potencial de chuvas intensas em todo o estado, com acumulados que podem somar 30 mm por hora ou 50 mm por dia.

🔎 O Simepar adota uma tabela para interpretar a força dos temporais. Se em um período de 6 horas chove menos de 0,2 mm, a chuva sequer é considerada. Entre 0,3 mm e 2,5 mm, é considerada um chuvisco. Se torna uma chuva fraca quando o acumulado em 6 horas é entre 2,5 mm e 10 mm. A partir daí até 25 mm, a chuva é moderada. Dos 25 mm aos 50 mm é considerada chuva forte, e acima dos 50 mm é considerada chuva extrema.

A Climatempo indica que nestes dois últimos dias da semana os ventos podem chegar a até 60 km/h no estado: nesta quinta em todo estado, com rajadas ainda maiores na faixa norte , e na sexta apenas na faixa sul . Veja nos mapas abaixo.

Regiões em risco de temporais — Foto: Climatempo

A previsão do tempo por cidade pode ser conferida neste link . Veja, abaixo, o resumo da Climatempo para o estado:

➡️QUINTA-FEIRA (29): Muita atenção para áreas mais ao norte do estado, regiões de divisa com o estado de São Paulo, devido ao risco maior de chuva volumosa ao longo do dia. A faixa que vai de Cornélio Procópio a Santo Antônio da Platina e a faixa leste do estado, entre o litoral e a Região Metropolitana de Curitiba terá uma quinta-feira com mais nebulosidade e menos aberturas de sol. Não estão totalmente descartados alguns períodos de tempo mais firme, mas o sol, se aparecer, será entre muitas nuvens. Nas outras áreas do estado, as pancadas de chuva devem vir especialmente no período da tarde. Como a umidade e a nebulosidade seguem altas, as temperaturas não devem subir muito nesta quinta. Boa parte do Paraná terá máximas em torno de 22°C. A região mais quente é a faixa oeste do estado.

➡️SEXTA-FEIRA (30): A instabilidade diminui no norte, mas ainda há previsão de chuva em diferentes pontos do estado nesta sexta-feira. As áreas que merecem mais atenção são as regiões de divisa com Santa Catarina e a faixa leste do estado, inclusive Curitiba e Região Metropolitana, devido à condição de chuvas que, pontualmente, podem vir com trovoadas e ventos moderados. No geral, o estado terá sol entre nuvens no período da manhã e pancadas de chuva, com trovoadas no período da tarde, podendo se estender até a noite. Como a nebulosidade diminui, a temperatura volta a subir, especialmente na faixa norte. Mesmo assim, os termômetros não devem atingir os 30°C.

➡️SÁBADO (31): Os ventos de leste transportam umidade para o litoral do Paraná e região de Curitiba. A previsão indica cerca de 4 mm na capital e 3 mm em Ponta Grossa. Nas outras áreas do estado, até pode chover, mas com baixos volumes acumulados. No geral, o sábado terá predomínio de sol, e temperaturas em elevação, principalmente no oeste, noroeste e no norte, com máximas que podem chegar perto dos 30°C.

➡️DOMINGO (1º): A chuva enfraquece no estado. Os maiores acumulados previstos são de aproximadamente 5 mm em Campo Mourão, 4 mm em Maringá e 4 mm em Ponta Grossa, nada que atrapalhe atividades ao ar livre. Em Curitiba, a estimativa é de 3 mm. Destaque para temperaturas bastante elevadas no interior, e as áreas mais quentes do estado devem registrar máximas acima dos 30°C.

articles.title: Menina de 8 anos é atacada por lobo em zoológico na Alemanha | G1
articles.standfirst: Criança participava de atividade especial dentro da jaula dos animais. Tratadora evitou que outras duas meninas fossem atacadas pela alcateia. Polícia investiga se houve negligência.
articles.summary: Criança participava de atividade especial dentro da jaula dos animais. Tratadora evitou que outras duas meninas fossem atacadas pela alcateia. Polícia investiga se houve negligência.
articles.body:
Parque de Vida Selvagem Johannismühle foi fechado após ataque de lobos — Foto: Carsten Koall/dpa/picture alliance

Uma menina de oito anos foi atacada nesta quarta-feira (28/10) por pelo menos um lobo num parque zoológico, localizado numa floresta próximo a Berlim, na Alemanha. Segundo a polícia, no momento do ataque, a criança estava dentro da jaula dos lobos com uma tratadora de animais e outras duas crianças.

A menina ficou gravemente ferida e foi transferida de helicóptero para um hospital.

O ataque ocorreu no Parque de Vida Selvagem Johannismühle, localizado em Baruth/Mark, a 45 quilômetros ao sul de Berlim. Segundo o distrito de Teltow-Fläming, o ataque ocorreu durante um programa especial para crianças. "O incidente aconteceu antes da abertura regular do parque, durante um dia de atividades com tratadores de animais para crianças", informou.

De acordo com o site do parque, os visitantes podem acompanhar o trabalho dos tratadores. Atualmente, diversos estados alemães estão em férias escolares de outono. As autoridades distritais anunciaram que vão revisar amplamente as condições de segurança do parque. O local permanecerá fechado.

A polícia também está investigando o ataque. Como as crianças tiveram acesso ao recinto ainda precisa ser esclarecido, disse o porta-voz policial. A investigação apura se houve negligência. "As circunstâncias exatas do ocorrido são objeto das investigações policiais."

A polícia informou inicialmente que a menina de oito anos estava pela manhã em um recinto de animais junto com outras duas crianças e uma funcionária. Em seguida, ela teria sido atacada por pelo menos um animal selvagem. Mais tarde, um porta-voz confirmou que se tratava de um lobo.

Ataque ocorreu durante atividade na jaula de lobos-do-ártico — Foto: Lubos Chlubny/Zoonar/picture alliance

Mais tarde a administração da região revelou mais detalhes da tragédia. O ataque aconteceu na área destinada aos lobos-do-ártico. "Enquanto os animais recebiam água no recinto, os lobos mantidos no local atacaram uma menina e a feriram gravemente", informou o distrito. A tratadora teria evitado, com uma reação rápida, que as outras duas meninas também fossem atacadas.

Quatro pessoas, entre elas três crianças, receberam atendimento de apoio psicológico de emergência.

O zoológico não quis comentar o caso. "Estamos cooperando integralmente com todas as autoridades", afirmou o parque. Por causa dos procedimentos em andamento, não seriam fornecidas mais informações. "Lamentamos profundamente o incidente, e a família afetada conta com todo o nosso apoio."

Inaugurado em 1997 numa área de mais de 100 hectares, o parque zoológico privado abriga cerca de 500 animas de 50 espécies, entre elas lobos, ursos e linces.

O distrito anunciou que revisará as normas de segurança e os procedimentos operacionais do parque. A reabertura do local só ocorrerá após autorização da autoridade competente.

O serviço veterinário também pretende realizar uma inspeção relacionada ao bem-estar animal no parque. "Até o momento, não há uma avaliação técnica sobre o estado de saúde e o comportamento do lobo, ou dos lobos possivelmente envolvidos, em relação ao incidente."

Segundo o distrito, a licença de operação do parque estabelece exigências específicas para a segurança e o estado das instalações onde os animais são mantidos. Uma inspeção realizada em 23 de julho de 2025 não constatou falhas de segurança relevantes em cercas ou barreiras de contenção. Conforme informado pelo parque na ocasião, as cercas consideradas essenciais para a segurança são verificadas todas as manhãs antes da abertura para detectar eventuais danos.

articles.title: Volkswagen tem prejuízo de US$ 6,5 bilhões, o maior em mais de 10 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Montadora alemã foi afetada por baixa contábil ligada à Porsche e enfrenta pressão de rivais chineses, tarifas e custos elevados com veículos elétricos.
articles.summary: Montadora alemã foi afetada por baixa contábil ligada à Porsche e enfrenta pressão de rivais chineses, tarifas e custos elevados com veículos elétricos.
articles.body:
Divulgação Volks — Foto: Divulgação Volks

A Volkswagen registrou prejuízo operacional de US$ 6,59 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, o pior resultado em mais de uma década. A montadora enfrenta dificuldades em mercados importantes, como a China, e iniciou uma ampla reestruturação dos negócios.

O resultado foi afetado por itens extraordinários que somaram cerca de US$ 8,9 bilhões, em grande parte relacionados a uma baixa contábil no valor da participação da Volkswagen na Porsche.

A receita de vendas da montadora também caiu 6% no terceiro trimestre, para US$ 87,1 bilhões.

Após a divulgação dos resultados, as ações da Volkswagen caíam 2%.

A empresa enfrenta uma concorrência cada vez mais acirrada na China, onde disputa espaço com fabricantes locais, além de custos bilionários com tarifas comerciais. Na Europa, a montadora também enfrenta gastos elevados para ampliar sua atuação no mercado de veículos elétricos, enquanto fabricantes chineses avançam na região.

➡️ Diante das dificuldades, o presidente-executivo da Volkswagen, Oliver Blume, planeja cortar 100 mil empregos em todo o grupo, que inclui marcas como Audi e Porsche. Até quatro fábricas na Alemanha correm risco de fechamento.

O plano enfrenta forte oposição dos sindicatos, que consideram possíveis greves a partir do início de 2027.

Em declaração em vídeo, o diretor financeiro da Volkswagen, Arno Antlitz, afirmou que os resultados dos nove primeiros meses do ano mostram a necessidade de acelerar as mudanças na empresa.

“Não podemos nos dar ao luxo de perder tempo. Precisamos agir com rapidez e determinação”, disse.

Antlitz também destacou que a margem operacional da Volkswagen nos nove primeiros meses do ano foi de apenas 3,8%, mesmo antes de considerar os itens extraordinários.

“Isso não é suficiente a longo prazo”, afirmou.

Em setembro, a Volkswagen já havia sinalizado custos extraordinários de cerca de US$ 11,2 bilhões e reduzido sua previsão de margem de lucro para 2026. A empresa passou a projetar um percentual máximo de 1%.

articles.title: RAF base chemical contamination worst in UK, report finds
articles.summary: Testing at RAF Upper Heyford finds "unacceptable" levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
articles.body:
Chemical contamination at a former RAF base earmarked for 9,000 homes is the worst found in the UK, a report has said.

Testing at RAF Upper Heyford carried out on behalf of a developer found "unacceptable" levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), referred to as forever chemicals.

Fears have been raised previously that the site could be the source of pollution in nearby waterways, after earlier testing by campaigners and the Environment Agency.

Paul Silver, chief executive of developer Dorchester Living, said separate soil samples taken from residential areas showed the area was "safe for use".

PFAS are a group of thousands of man-made chemicals , some of which can cause cancer, which are often referred to as forever chemicals because they do not break down easily.

The results of the site investigations were uploaded to Cherwell District Council's website as part of a planning application.

The author of the report said they were higher than the village of Bentham, Yorkshire, "determined as having the highest level of PFAS in the UK ".

The Environment Agency (EA) said military sites and airports were hotspots for PFAS, which were used extensively in firefighting foams for decades.

At RAF Upper Heyford, firefighters would practice putting out an aeroplane set on fire above a "pond" of fuel.

This training area was found to be "the most significant ongoing source of PFAS contamination identified".

Another report into ground and surface water found contamination was "widespread" at the site, with all samples exceeding environmental standards.

Subsequent independent testing by Gallos Brook Environmental Group found elevated levels of the chemicals in more than a dozen streams that flow from beneath the base.

The results have prompted concerns from residents about existing and approved developments near the site, including a primary school.

Groundwater and surface water results from the school site in another report showed PFAS exceeded safe levels by environmental quality standards.

Calum Miller, MP for Bicester and Woodstock, said: "The most important thing is to understand fully what level of contamination, if any, there is in that area.

"And in the case of a primary school that people have real confidence that it's a safe environment for children."

The BBC has spoken to residents living near the site who would like their blood tested to determine if they have been disproportionately exposed.

One of them, Leigh Radwell, said she was concerned for her health after eating vegetables from her garden.

She said: "My little countryside haven and my dream of growing my own veg and having chickens and supporting wildlife is ruined.

Helen Christie, from Gallos Brook Environmental Group, said the results confirmed what campaigners had been saying: "That the site is contaminated."

But she said the testing done so far had been "inadequate".

"The duty of care now must be towards the 1,300 houses already built and those living in the surrounding areas," she added.

The report carried out for Dorchester Living said the PFAS contamination could be managed through a phased remediation approach.

CEO Paul Silver said: "This testing was the first step and an outline strategy for further investigation has been submitted as part of the planning application.

"We anticipate that this will include further investigation work on a phased basis with any necessary remediation to be secured through the planning process."

He continued: "The levels of contamination found on site are significantly lower than we had expected given its historic use. Soil samples taken from residential areas show that homes are safe for use"

The results of these further tests have not been made public.

Silver added: "We continue to recognise our responsibilities as a landowner and developer and are continuing to work with the Cherwell District Council, Environment Agency and other relevant government bodies."

The local authority previously called on the government to support it on the issue and a working group has been set up alongside the developer and the Environment Agency.

Cherwell District Council has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Fuel prices blamed for diesel theft from Worcester haulier
articles.summary: The fuel was stolen from two vehicles at the weekend, the director of M Pinches & Sons Ltd said.
articles.body:
A West Midlands haulage company has said thieves are motivated by rising fuel prices after they stole 400 litres of diesel.

Martin Pinches, director of M Pinches & Sons Ltd in Worcester, said the fuel was stolen from two vehicles at the weekend.

"[It happened] because of the price of fuel," he claimed, adding that it was "an added cost that everyone has been burdened with."

Pinches said fuel had become "liquid gold" and estimated the missing diesel was worth about £800.

Because we're a business, and we use more fuel, it's a bigger burden on us really," he added.

"It's always a bit disappointing, isn't it?"

Pinches said the thieves also broke numerous fuel sending units and fuel caps on the vehicles, resulting in lost revenue as they were out of action for a day being repaired.

West Mercia Police told the BBC it had "received a report of a burglary after a business was broken into sometime between 24 and 25 October.

A force spokesperson said: "It was reported that a large quantity of fuel was stolen from two lorries on the site. Inquiries are ongoing."

During Wednesday's budget, Chancellor John Healey said the 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, would be extended to July. It was scheduled to be phased out from January.

It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52p per litre.

Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.

The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February. A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.

Pinches said something like this happening again is "always in the back of your mind".

"[To prevent it] we will maybe tell the drivers not to fill the lorries up until the morning they're going out".

articles.title: Northumberland's new data centres must bring 'local benefits'
articles.summary: As "strict tests" are floated, Northumberland waits to see if three data centres will spring up.
articles.body:
Government plans to impose "strict tests" on data centres before they can be built have received a cautious welcome in an area which could soon be home to three such facilities.

During Wednesday's Budget speech, Chancellor John Healey said new centres would face requirements to "invest in local communities, create local jobs and protect local water supplies".

The Conservative leader of Northumberland County Council, which gave US firm QTS the go-ahead for a £10bn facility at Cambois and is considering two more applications, said the sector was "absolutely critical" for the economy.

Meanwhile, the local Labour MP welcomed Healey's pledge but warned the "devil is in the detail".

Last month, Blyth and Ashington MP Ian Lavery called on the prime minister to regulate data centre developments like those in his constituency, fearing they would take up "scarce industrial land that could be used for other industries that create far more local jobs".

On Wednesday, the chancellor told the House of Commons: "When the NHS uses AI to treat patients, we want that data here, when our armed forces use AI to keep us safe, we want that data here."

He said if companies invested locally, created jobs and protected resources, they "will get the grid connections they need and, where necessary, be allowed to build onsite generation while they wait".

Speaking to the Local Democracy Reporting Service afterwards, Lavery said: "We have to listen to the residents much more than we have been."

He said the chancellor's pledge "broadly speaking does address the issues" being raised, but he was "not sure it could cover the impact of having three or four data centres within two square miles".

Northumberland County Council leader Glen Sanderson said of the QTS plans: "If it is done right and carefully then data centre development is absolutely crucial for a new economy and a new generation of people."

articles.title: Small businesses in Bilston say Budget failed to deliver the help they need
articles.summary: People in Bilston react to the new Budget set out by Chancellor John Healey.
articles.body:
"We need more help for small businesses instead of punishing them," said butcher Kevin Evans, in response to the government's new tax and spending plans.

In the Budget, set out by Chancellor John Healey on Wednesday, a number of measures were announced, including a one-off £100 payment for up to 20 million households in council tax bands A-D in England.

However, for those living and working in Bilston, Wolverhampton, not enough is being done to tackle the rising cost of living.

"The electricity is a killer, it's a big one, it's mega money. It's just out of control now," added Kevin Evans, a butcher and business owner.

"Six sausages would have cost you £1.50 last year, but it's around £2.50 now."

The Budget also included a 3.9% rise in the legal minimum wage from April, as well as a new flat-rate state pension increase of £488 a year, equivalent to 3.9%, under the triple lock policy. The old basic state pension will rise by £374.40.

Watch: What are the key points from the Budget and how will they be funded?

Will I get the £100 energy payment and when will I receive it?

Evans told BBC Radio WM the measures would make things harder for his business, not easier.

He added: "I would love to take another person on but I can't afford to because National Insurance and the minimum wage keep going up. I might as well just do the hours myself.

"You have less time at home. I don't get a day off now. It's not feasible, it comes out of my pocket which is already being emptied.

"It doesn't benefit you to be a businessman in this country anymore."

The sentiment was echoed by plasterer Glen Gandy, who said he also could not afford to expand his workforce or absorb the rising cost of materials.

The father-of-two said: "There is nothing in the new Budget that will help my business.

"Minimum wage up by 3.9% is good for kids, but you're going to employ someone with more experience if you have to pay them extra anyway, so it will push people out of work.

"We haven't put our wages up for two and a half years to absorb the costs, but there is nothing you can do about the materials.

"I pay around £350 a week on fuel just going around Wolverhampton. It costs us a fortune."

Lutfu Efe, who owns a chip shop, said he now pays nearly £800 a month for electricity and £600 a month for gas.

"This is why we are struggling. Many years ago it was around £300, but it has sky-rocketed," he said.

"It's not just me, everyone is in the same boat. Everything has gone up. We have two options: the government helps us or we have to close down.

"There is nothing in this Budget to help me."

For households across England, Scotland and Wales, standing charges, fixed daily fees customers pay regardless of usage, will be removed from gas bills, while the VAT cut on electricity bills has been extended until July.

Import taxes are to be removed on more than 100 food products, including gherkins and marmalade, as well as kerosene and fertilisers.

For mum-of-six Gwyneth Totney, the one-off £100 payment will "help but not much, it will cover about two weeks of gas and electric".

She added: "My weekly shop has gone from about £100 to about £130 a week.

"I've started going to the butcher's for my meat now as it's cheaper than the supermarket.

"We're working more to get more money but we have less time. We still have our pizza night and cinema night at home, but it's way too expensive to take all the kids to the cinema."

Reacting to the Budget, she said: "It feels like they are trying to bring the cost of living down, but they are not actually doing it."

articles.title: Rare Narnia book sold in Cornwall charity shop sells for £1k
articles.summary: A volunteer spotted a first edition of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe "completely by chance".
articles.body:
A rare first edition of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe has sold for £1,000 after it was spotted at a charity shop.

The 1950 copy of the first of the Chronicles of Narnia by CS Lewis was identified by a sharp-eyed volunteer at the Oxfam bookshop in Truro, Cornwall.

The children's fantasy novel was put up for sale on the charity's online selling portal and was quickly snapped up.

Store manager Barnaby Attwell said: "It's great to know that money will be going to help people in need."

The Chronicles of Narnia is a series of seven novels - the most famous being The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe - published between 1950 and 1956.

They have been the subject of multiple screen and stage adaptations, most recently a Netflix production of The Chronicles of Narnia.

Jane Rickard said she had been sorting through some newly donated books when she came across the rare volume "completely by chance".

"It looked like an old copy of it, I looked inside to see if it was a reprint, and it wasn't, and I got quite excited," she recalled.

"So I checked online for what a first edition would look like and that's when I thought, 'It's a first edition!'"

The volunteer worker said "my jaw dropped" when she realised what the book might be worth, adding: "For us, it's very unusual.

"We do get some excellent donations, and it's not that rare to have a £30 book, a £50 book, but £1,000 has never happened.

"I can only think it was the magic of Narnia because there was no reason for me to even be looking at that section - I'm normally behind the counter or in the shop. It just looked like a small hardback book."

Barnaby Attwell, manager of Oxfam Books Truro, said he was amazed "when Jane plucked the book out amongst many other similar-looking books".

"Another volunteer looked it up and saw that, even without a dust jacket, a first edition is worth over a thousand pounds.

"A couple of other volunteers checked it too and we all agreed.

"Another volunteer wrote a description of it, and I photographed it and put it online for £1,000. So it was a real collaborative effort."

Attwell said "we were all over the moon" when the book sold.

"I haven't stopped thanking Jane, and gave her a bunch of flowers at our shop general meeting recently," he said.

"It's great to know that money will be going to help people in need."

articles.title: Bury St Edmunds pitstop for the busker cycling with a piano
articles.summary: James Tofalli is cycling from Land's End to John O'Groats in a bid to make pianos accessible to all.
articles.body:
A busker who is cycling across the country with an upright piano in tow has taken his foot off the pedals in Suffolk.

James Tofalli, known as the Piano Man, tickled the ivories during a brief stop off in Bury St Edmunds.

The pianist set off from Land's End in Cornwall on 11 July and has been joined on the 874-mile (1,407 km) cycle to John O'Groats by his faithful cocker spaniel, Jeff.

Tofalli told BBC Radio Suffolk his aim was to bring smiles to people's faces, raise awareness of mental health and autism, and eradicate barriers to music by campaigning for more pianos to be installed in public spaces.

"People are surprised, shocked and confused at the route I'm taking, but the majority of responses are positive, and that's the joy of what street music is," he said.

"I've busked in Bury St Edmunds a lot in the past and it is a great place to play - I've had a lot of positive experiences, but for me Bury is a big part of this journey."

Tofalli, who has battled homelessness and mental health issues, first started taking his music seriously after plucking up the courage to have a go on a public piano at London's St Pancras station 10 years ago.

At the time he said he was battling an addiction, but having a musical outlet gave him an "opportunity to phase that addiction out and bring the piano in".

He credits public pianos with helping him to "overcome addiction and find his footing with ADHD".

"I still get nervous playing, but it is a happy excitement and I've done what I've set out to do and that's bring music to people," he added.

"I can't even put it into words [how the piano changed my life] - I genuinely wouldn't be here today without playing the piano."

Tofalli first set himself the challenge of travelling the country on his purpose-built cargo bike in 2021, but his trip was curtailed when he was stopped by police.

He said he was subsequently charged with illegally "driving a piano" on the A92 in Arbroath, Scotland.

This time, therefore, he is even more determined to cross the finish line – although when that will be remains a "work in progress".

"Loads of people have done Land's End to John O'Groats, cycling or walking in many different ways," he said.

"And I believe it had been done with a keyboard, but nobody's ever done it with a full upright piano with an iron frame."

Tofalli said his mission was to raise money to "acquire, refurbish, place and maintain pianos in public spaces, town squares, stations, parks, community hubs and family homes".

He is funding the journey himself by busking in towns and cities along the way.

"The idea is to give people the opportunity I had when I was struggling with addiction," he added.

"There's no-one to say, 'You can't try it, you can't have a go', even if you go up and just press a few notes – there's no barriers, there's no boundaries."

The Piano Man's efforts went down well with people in Bury St Edmunds - not least Steven Hooper, who has seen him busk before and always gives him £20.

"He has come a long way with his mental health and everything else and he is just spectacular, to just sit here and play music to everyone is unbelievable," he said.

"I had not seen him for a while, but then I saw his face and I came over - it's lovely and just brilliant."

articles.title: Jet2 pilot flies daughter and Framlingham students to Iceland
articles.summary: Marnie Munns says it was "a huge privilege" to fly her daughter's school party to Reykjavik.
articles.body:
An airline pilot had some special passengers aboard her plane when she flew her daughter, classmates and teachers to Iceland for a school trip.

Marnie Munns, from Cambridge, captained the Jet2 flight from Stansted Airport to Reykjavik with her 17-year-old daughter Lillian and about 30 others from Framlingham College, Suffolk, on board.

She managed to swap a shift to make sure she could be in the cockpit for the flight on Monday.

"It isn't every day you get to go to Iceland, and it certainly isn't every day your mum flies you there," said Lillian.

Munns said it was a "huge privilege" to be at the controls of the Airbus A321neo with her daughter and her fellow pupils on board.

She had initially planned on surprising geography student Lillian on the morning of the flight but had to come clean during a parents' evening.

"When I first told her I was doing it, she couldn't believe that I was actually going to do it and had followed through on it," said Munns.

"Pilots will try to fly their family because it is such a unique experience and it is just a real pleasure, so it was nice to have a really lovely, personal day out."

Lillian's party were joined on the 232-seater's full flight by pupils and staff from other schools embarking on a similar trip.

Her teachers were not the only people excited to learn who the pilot would be.

"What surprised me was the excitement of my fellow crew members when I told them I had the pleasure of flying my daughter and had the whole school trip on board," said Munns.

"The first officer was so excited about it and the crew were fantastic and they found out where she was sitting and it was really nice and quite funny."

Munns has been a captain for 19 years but had never flown her daughter on a commercial flight before.

She said while she tried to do her best on every flight, she did feel added pressure when flying her daughter – especially in making the flight announcements, as Lillian was keen for a "shout-out".

"I was mindful we had many other schools on board, and so I wanted to make sure everyone felt they were special to be on the flight, but of course, my daughter," she said.

"Jet2 gives me an aircraft to be in control of, and it's a big plane, so to do that with my daughter and her school, in style, was quite special."
